label: Order
title: Order & availability
benefit: Make realistic promises and identify overselling earlier.
scope: What can we reliably promise the customer?

questions.q: Can I still sell 100 Olive Cups?
questions.method: Subtract active reservations from physical stock. Show promised receipts separately until goods have actually been received.
questions.need: Item ID, stock snapshot, active reservations and open supply commitments.
questions.result: Available quantity, shortfall and evidence for the current state.

questions.q: Which open orders can be fulfilled entirely from available stock?
questions.method: Check each open line against stock and allocated reservations. Allocate the same units to only one order.
questions.need: Open order lines, reservation allocations and current stock per warehouse.
questions.result: Orders classified as fully fulfillable, partially fulfillable or blocked, with reasons.

questions.q: Which orders have a mismatch between promised and reserved quantities?
questions.method: Compare the current order quantity with active reservations per line. Account for canceled and shipped quantities.
questions.need: Order changes, lines, reservations, cancellations and recorded shipments.
questions.result: Variance per order and line, including missing or excess quantities.

questions.q: Which open orders are affected by a delayed incoming delivery?
questions.method: Link the changed receipt commitment to open customer orders through items and allocations. Mark the impact as unresolved where allocations are missing.
questions.need: Versioned receipt commitment, item links, order allocations and customer deadlines.
questions.result: Affected orders and commitments at risk, for manual review.

label: Delivery
title: Delivery & customer communication
benefit: Identify delivery problems earlier and help customers with evidence-backed information.
scope: What is happening to the goods on their way to the customer?
sources: Shop · DHL / DPD / UPS · Customer communication

questions.q: Where are my parcels, and which need attention?
questions.method: Combine the latest carrier status with the order, scan time and reported forecast. Keep older scans visible in history.
questions.need: Order-to-shipment links, carrier scans and available delivery forecasts.
questions.result: Shipment overview with last known status and issues requiring attention.

questions.q: Which customer delivery commitments are overdue or at risk?
questions.method: Compare the customer commitment with actual shipping or delivery status. Label carrier forecasts as estimates.
questions.need: Explicit customer commitment, time zone, shipment status and any carrier forecast.
questions.result: Prioritized cases with the promised date, current state and explanation.

questions.q: Which partial deliveries still have missing items?
questions.method: Compare ordered quantities per line with confirmed partial deliveries. Handle canceled lines and shipping labels without shipment confirmation separately.
questions.need: Order lines, partial deliveries, included quantities and handover/delivery events.
questions.result: Outstanding quantities per order and the associated shipments.

questions.q: What can I reliably tell this customer about their delivery status?
questions.method: Use the order, latest scans and prior promises to draft a reply. Explicitly leave unknown arrival dates unresolved.
questions.need: Customer-to-order links, carrier history and prior communication.
questions.result: Customer-friendly draft with internal evidence; sending remains a separate action.

label: Invoice
title: Invoice & receivables
benefit: Find missing documents and understand the current receivables balance.
scope: What has the customer been invoiced for?

questions.q: Which invoices are still outstanding?
questions.method: Calculate each invoice state from its original amount, corrections and reported payments. Do not sum superseded states again.
questions.need: Invoice, correction documents, reported payment status and due date.
questions.result: Outstanding amounts and due dates with an evidence chain; payment markers are not bank evidence.

questions.q: Which orders still need an invoice under our invoicing rule?
questions.method: Evaluate orders against the configured invoicing rule, for example after shipment. Reconcile linked invoices and cancellations.
questions.need: Invoicing rule, order/delivery status, invoice links and complete import coverage.
questions.result: Review list of potentially missing invoices; status remains unknown when data is incomplete.

questions.q: Where does the invoice amount differ from the agreed order amount?
questions.method: Compare lines, quantities, discounts, shipping charges, currency and stated taxes. Account for partial invoices.
questions.need: Versioned order and invoice lines, including partial-invoice references.
questions.result: Amount difference per line with a traceable reconciliation explanation.

questions.q: Which invoices were created but have no evidence of being sent?
questions.method: Link created documents to the invoicing tool's sending event. With incomplete sending data, report missing evidence only.
questions.need: Invoice ID, creation time, sending status and last synchronization time.
questions.result: Documents without sending evidence, including data freshness rather than an unsupported conclusion that they were not sent.

label: Customer payment
title: Customer payment & resolution
benefit: Resolve payment issues precisely and avoid unnecessary payment reminders.
scope: Has the customer made their payment?
sources: Shop / Invoice · Payment provider · Payment evidence

questions.q: Which orders are only authorized, actually paid or still awaiting payment?
questions.method: Read authorizations, successful captures and failed attempts separately. Show order status alongside transaction status.
questions.need: Order ID, unique transaction reference, amount, currency and latest payment status.
questions.result: Payment status per order with evidence; an authorization does not count as a capture.

questions.q: Which failed payments have since been completed successfully?
questions.method: Order all attempts for the same order chronologically. Account for a later success without removing the failure from history.
questions.need: Payment attempts sharing an order reference and a confirmed captured amount.
questions.result: Outstanding payment issues separated from resolved cases.

questions.q: Which invoices have a mismatch between partial payments and the remaining amount?
questions.method: Reconcile allocated customer payments and correction documents against the receivable. Do not treat provider fees as a customer payment shortfall.
questions.need: Invoice, payment allocations, gross amounts, currencies and correction documents.
questions.result: Remaining amount or overpayment with calculation; unallocated payments shown separately.

questions.q: Which due receivables should Finance review today?
questions.method: Prioritize by due date and outstanding amount. Account for reported payments, ongoing investigations and agreed deadlines.
questions.need: Receivables balance, due date, received payments, resolution status and applicable reminder rules.
questions.result: Evidence-backed review list with reasons and open questions. No automatic payment reminder.

label: Payout
title: Payout & bank reconciliation
benefit: Understand where the money is and which differences remain unresolved.
scope: Has the captured money reached our bank account?
sources: Payment provider · Payout report · Bank evidence

questions.q: Where is my money across payment providers?
questions.method: Separate processing, available, held, in-transit and bank-confirmed amounts. Count only the current state per provider.
questions.need: Transactions, fees, holds, refunds, payouts and separate bank evidence.
questions.result: Evidence-backed money positions per provider. A payout is not new revenue.

questions.q: Why is the payout lower than captured customer payments?
questions.method: Break down the transactions included in the payout report: captures minus fees, refunds and other evidenced deductions.
questions.need: Payout reference and a complete list of included transactions and adjustments.
questions.result: Gross-to-net reconciliation; any remaining difference is explicitly unresolved.

questions.q: Which announced or sent payouts still lack bank evidence?
questions.method: Distinguish announcements from actual payout transfers. Match transferred amounts to bank entries by reference, amount and currency.
questions.need: Payout status, reference, amount, currency, bank entries and their import coverage.
questions.result: Missing confirmations with age and data freshness; no conclusion about bank receipt without bank data.

questions.q: Which amounts are held, and which releases are only announced?
questions.method: Show active holds and pending release commitments separately from actual releases. Do not add historical holds together.
questions.need: Provider balances, hold reason, status changes and any release dates.
questions.result: Held amounts by provider and reason; expected dates explicitly labeled as commitments.

label: Reversal
title: Cancellation, return & refund
benefit: Resolve outstanding reversals and prevent duplicate refunds.
scope: What still needs to happen after a cancellation or return?
sources: Shop / Returns system · Invoicing tool · Provider

questions.q: Which returns are announced, received or already refunded?
questions.method: Treat the return request, actual goods receipt, document correction and cash refund as separate steps.
questions.need: Return ID, order lines, return-shipment status, goods receipt and refund reference.
questions.result: State per return with the next unresolved step. An announcement does not confirm goods receipt.

questions.q: Which credit notes are missing their corresponding refund?
questions.method: Link credit notes to the original payment state and refunds. A credit note can reduce an outstanding receivable without returning money.
questions.need: Credit note, original customer payment, refund entitlement and provider evidence.
questions.result: Only genuinely outstanding refund cases, separated from receivable-only corrections.

questions.q: What still needs correcting in stock, invoicing and payment after a cancellation?
questions.method: Reconcile the cancellation with reservation release, document correction and payment reversal. Recognize steps already completed.
questions.need: Cancellation event, reservation history, invoice documents and payment/refund status.
questions.result: Evidence-backed checklist of outstanding steps per order; no automatic posting.

questions.q: Is there a risk of duplicate repayment through both a refund and a chargeback?
questions.method: Link refunds and chargebacks actually booked by the provider to the same original transaction. Treat open disputes separately.
questions.need: Original transaction, refund IDs, chargeback postings, amounts and statuses.
questions.result: Suspected cases for review with an amount comparison. An open dispute alone is not a repayment.
